notes: AI-generated persona goals (3) and barriers (3) per participant, grounded in their tagged segments.
Each item carries 1–2 supporting_segment_ids and optionally one subtheme_id.
supporting_segment_ids are constrained to the participant's own segments at generation time.

goals.summary: Stay on some form of GLP-1 for life to protect the maintenance weight she's held since 15.
Join a trial for a longer-acting injectable or implant to help future maintenance patients like her.
Keep a cheaper backup plan ready, eyeing semaglutide, orforglipron, or vetted compounders if Zepbound becomes unaffordable.

barriers.summary: Zepbound's US price could force her off it if continuing would financially harm her family.
Landing on a trial placebo would risk regaining the weight she's kept off since age 15.
An oral GLP-1's strict timing-and-food rules would trip her up versus her current weekly shot.

goals.summary: Stay on some dose of Tirzepatide long-term to protect the inflammation, sleep apnea, and teeth-grinding gains he's already seen.
Move to next-generation GLP-1s as the science evolves, having already tracked first- and second-gen options closely.
Contribute to GLP-1 research as a pro-science participant if a trial fits around his heavy work travel schedule.

barriers.summary: Fears losing Tirzepatide access if US policy or insurance coverage shifts, even though he's stable on it now.
Frequent work travel makes in-person trial visits and at-home nurse appointments hard to commit to a week out.
Wants clearer answers on adverse-event medical coverage and compounding pharmacy sourcing before fully trusting a trial drug.

goals.summary: Hold onto the inflammation, sleep apnea, and teeth-grinding wins he's seen in three months on tirzepatide.
Stay ahead of the next-generation GLP-1s and switch when a better-fitting injectable reaches market.
Contribute to GLP-1 science as a willing trial participant since friends are already enrolled.

barriers.summary: Heavy work travel makes fixed clinic visits and at-home nurse appointments nearly impossible to commit to.
Fears US policy or supply shifts could cut off his tirzepatide access mid-treatment.
Lacks clarity on who covers care if a trial drug triggers a serious adverse event like a heart issue.

goals.summary: Stay on compounded GLP-1 long-term to protect the blood pressure and heartburn improvements she's already gained.
Transition to the upcoming Orforglipron maintenance pill once it's FDA-approved to avoid weekly injections she dislikes.
Contribute to GLP-1 research as a master's-trained academic, ideally through a locally-run trial near her town.

barriers.summary: Her PBM won't even speak to her doctor's office, leaving a $1,000/month out-of-pocket cost she can't sustain.
The only Eli Lilly trial she qualified for is a three-hour drive each way from where she lives.
Eight to ten weekly hours for clinic visits, counseling, and injections is impossible alongside her busy life.

goals.summary: Stay on compound tirzepatide for life since GLP-1s were her last hope after decades of obesity since age 12.
Get into a cutting-edge trial like Retatrutide to help advance obesity treatment after being rejected once already.
Switch or stack GLP-1s with her doctor's help to break stalls, the way compounding recently restarted her loss.

barriers.summary: Affordability and supply shortages dictate her med choice, pushing her to compound tirzepatide instead of brand Mounjaro.
Living rural with Atlanta an hour away makes frequent trial visits unworkable unless monthly or transportation is arranged.
Worries about being a guinea pig for unknown side effects beyond the usual GLP-1 gastric issues.

goals.summary: Protect the GLP-1 quality-of-life gains — better sleep, lower blood pressure, quieter food noise — that finally stuck after years of failed diets.
Stay on top of emerging GLP-1 options, hoping for monthly dosing or an oral version with equal efficacy.
Join a trial that guarantees continued medication access and offers evidence-based nutrition guidance over gimmicks like meal replacements.

barriers.summary: Worries employer insurance could drop coverage, leaving a $1,000+ monthly out-of-pocket cost he couldn't justify long term.
Frequent work travel makes monthly in-person clinic visits and half-day appointment blocks logistically unworkable for trial participation.
Fears being randomized into a placebo arm and regaining weight, erasing the mental and physical benefits he's built.

goals.summary: Stay on the current GLP-1 long-term to protect the quiet-from-food-noise relief and reduced knee inflammation.
Join a trial only if telehealth visits and monthly injections fit around an unpredictable work schedule.
Get real obesity-literate support like nutrition coaching and post-medication maintenance guidance, not just 'eat less' advice.

barriers.summary: Constant anxiety that insurance changes or GLP-1 shortages could yank away the medication that finally worked.
Fear of being randomized to placebo and rapidly regaining weight, reviving the old shame cycle.
Years of keto, Weight Watchers, and bootcamps that failed left a residue of self-blame around weight loss.
